issues.legal_issue: A court deciding a suit founded on title must determine whether the plaintiff proved title before granting relief based on possession.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed ownership and possession and sought a permanent injunction against interference with possession.
The defendant denied both the plaintiff’s title and possession and asserted that the land was public land.
The plaintiff did not produce the sale deed on which the claimed title was based.
The appellate court treated title as admitted and relied on possession and revenue entries without determining whether the plaintiff had proved title.
issues.conclusion: The appellate court committed a substantial error of law by decreeing the suit without deciding the disputed claim of title; its judgment could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit based on title, the plaintiff bears the burden of proving title, and the court must decide that issue before granting relief. A claim of possession does not dispense with that inquiry where title is disputed. Revenue mutation entries do not themselves create title; Nirman Singh v. Lal Rudra Partab, 1926 PC 100, explains their fiscal character.

predicates.title_based_civil_suit: The plaintiff brought a civil suit claiming a right to the property and seeking relief on that basis.
predicates.title_denied: The defendant disputed the plaintiff’s claimed title to the property.
predicates.appellate_court_failed_to_determine_titl: The appellate court granted relief without deciding whether the plaintiff had proved the disputed title.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks relief in a title-based civil suit and the defendant disputes title, a decree cannot stand if the appellate court did not determine whether the plaintiff proved title.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking an injunction on the basis of claimed ownership and continuing possession cannot be treated as a summary suit for recovery of possession when the plaintiff did not allege dispossession.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed to be the owner and to remain in possession of the land.
The plaintiff sought a permanent injunction against interference with possession and did not allege that the defendant had dispossessed him.
Both parties presented evidence on title as well as possession.
issues.conclusion: The suit could not be treated as one for recovery of possession based on prior possession and dispossession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 provides a summary remedy to a person dispossessed from immovable property otherwise than in due course of law. The plaintiff must rely on prior possession and dispossession, rather than assert continuing possession and seek an injunction on the basis of ownership. The provision corresponds to Section 9 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877. The principle that peaceful possession may be protected without determining title is discussed in Perry v. Clissold, 1907 AC 73, and Nair Service Society v. K.C. Alexander, AIR 1968 SC 1165.

rule.if: summary_possession_proceeding and plaintiff_claimed_continuing_possession and not plaintiff_alleged_dispossession

predicates.summary_possession_proceeding: The case is being considered as a summary proceeding to recover possession based on prior possession and dispossession.
predicates.plaintiff_claimed_continuing_possession: The plaintiff asserted that they remained in possession of the property.
predicates.plaintiff_alleged_dispossession: The plaintiff alleged that the defendant had dispossessed them from the property.

issues.definition: A case treated as a summary possession proceeding cannot be treated as a dispossession-based possession suit where the plaintiff claimed continuing possession and did not allege dispossession.

issues.legal_issue: Revenue mutation entries do not themselves establish title to property.
material_facts: The plaintiff relied on revenue entries made after the claimed purchase and during the pendency of an earlier suit.
The sale deed said to support the plaintiff’s title was not produced.
The appellate court relied on the revenue entries without determining whether the plaintiff had proved title.
issues.conclusion: The revenue entries did not establish title and could not justify decreeing the suit without proof of title.
issues.legal_principle: Mutation in revenue records is a fiscal inquiry for identifying the person from whom revenue may be collected; it is not a source of title. The court relied on Nirman Singh v. Lal Rudra Partab, 1926 PC 100. It also noted that entries made during the pendency of earlier litigation were of little consequence in the circumstances of this case.

predicates.title_claim_in_property_suit: A party in a property suit claims ownership of the disputed property.
predicates.title_based_on_mutation_entries: A party relies on mutation entries in revenue records as proof of ownership.

issues.definition: In a property suit, mutation entries relied on as proof of a claimed title do not establish that title.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court must interfere in a second appeal where the lower appellate court’s failure to decide a central title issue raises a substantial question of law.
material_facts: The trial court found that the plaintiff had not proved title or possession and dismissed the suit.
The lower appellate court reversed that decision without determining the disputed title and treated it as admitted despite the defendant’s denial.
The High Court dismissed the defendant’s second appeal in limine.
issues.conclusion: A substantial question of law arose, and the High Court should not have dismissed the second appeal in limine; the judgments of the lower appellate court and the High Court were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: A second appeal presents a substantial question of law when the lower appellate court fails to address the central disputed issue of title and proceeds on an erroneous assumption that title was admitted. The High Court should interfere in that circumstance; the Supreme Court distinguished the authorities cited on factual findings because the title issue had not been investigated.

predicates.second_appeal_from_property_suit: The proceeding is a second appeal arising from a property suit.
predicates.lower_appellate_court_ignored_disputed_t: The lower appellate court failed to determine a disputed title issue central to the suit.
predicates.high_court_dismissed_appeal_in_limine: The High Court dismissed the second appeal at the outset without examining it on its merits.

issues.definition: In a second appeal from a property suit, the High Court must interfere when the lower appellate court ignored disputed title and the High Court dismissed the appeal in limine.
